header.author: Incertus
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tmp1106.tmp1106.opp-lat1, from Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.urn:cts:latinLit:tmp1106.tmp1106.opp-lat: The opening 'egL.' is a garbled numeral, evidently CXL (the canons before and after are CXXXVIII and CXLI); '56' may likewise be a misprint. 'do- ricos' is read as clericos. 'Mathematicians' here are casters of horoscopes; 'phylacteries' are amulets.

nodes.text: [CXL]. — 56. That priests or clerics must not be magicians or enchanters, or mathematicians, or astrologers, or make what are called phylacteries, which are in fact bonds for the souls themselves. And those who wear them we order to be cast out of the church.
